ai.title: Large Language Models: A Plain-Language Overview for Engineers
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.34585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are neural networks trained on huge text collections to generate text by predicting what comes next. Engineers using ChatGPT and other generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools need a clear picture of what training changes and prompts add. The article starts with the Transformer, which connects words in context, and pre-training, where models learn to predict text. It then explains how fine-tuning adapts models to requests, with reinforcement learning from human feedback using human answer rankings. Next, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) supplies documents, while chain-of-thought prompting encourages intermediate steps and agents use tools. FlashAttention lowers training and running costs by reducing data movement during attention; quantized low-rank adaptation (QLoRA) saves fine-tuning memory. Readers get a life cycle figure and tables comparing methods and their limits. A short checklist for judging LLM evaluation claims flags test material in training (data contamination) and model-based grading (LLM-as-a-judge). It also covers very long inputs (long context) and hallucination, meaning false or unsupported claims. Check factual accuracy separately from whether an answer sounds helpful.
ai.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are neural networks trained on huge text collections to generate text by predicting what comes next.

ai.title: $M^3$: A Multi-LLM System for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.31937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to carefully orchestrated multi-turn interactions that progressively bypass safety mechanisms. However, many existing red-teaming approaches rely on heuristics or impose strong assumptions that limit their applicability in fully black box settings. We address this gap by introducing $M^3$, an automated red-teaming framework that formalizes multi-turn jailbreaking as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process (MDP). In $M^3$, an attacker LLM interacts with a target LLM while operating over a compact internal state produced by a state LLM. Across two benchmarks and six target models, $M^3$ consistently outperforms state-of-the-art multi-turn red-teaming methods in Attack Success Rates (ASR), achieving improvements of up to 53% in ASR@5. Even with lightweight attacker, $M^3$ attains gains up to 26% in ASR@1 and 34% in ASR@5, compared to baselines that use higher capacity attackers. Beyond improved effectiveness, $M^3$ exhibits steeper risk escalation over conversational turns and achieves more consistent performance across risk categories (up to 4.82 improvement in Gini index) without relying on predefined risk taxonomy, providing a scalable and principled framework for multi-turn red-teaming and safety evaluation.
ai.summary: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to carefully orchestrated multi-turn interactions that progressively bypass safety mechanisms.

ai.title: Understanding Communication Failures in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.32060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems aim to improve reasoning through debate, evidence sharing, and mutual correction, but interaction can also introduce failures that final accuracy alone cannot explain. Agents may converge too early, ignore dissent, suppress correct minority answers, or preserve a wrong framing across rounds. We present a corpus-grounded taxonomy of communication failures, built from 3,211 failed multi-round trajectories across medical QA, coding, finance, multi-hop reasoning, ethics, and embodied text tasks. Using this taxonomy, we analyze failure distributions across datasets and system designs, round-level error dynamics, recovery hardness, majority transitions, minority-signal suppression, and self-reported confidence. We find that failures are dominated by recovery/correction and consensus/decision problems rather than isolated first-round mistakes, with many emerging after agents first observe peer responses. Based on these findings, we recommend stronger disagreement handling, evidence verification, minority-signal preservation, and recovery checks before finalization.

ai.title: Training an MoE LLM in MXFP4: How We Closed the Gap to BF16
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.32229v2 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) in sub-8-bit arithmetic promises substantial gains in memory bandwidth and compute throughput, yet FP4 formats introduce quantization error severe enough to destabilize optimization if left unaddressed. We present ALTO, an open-source training recipe for GPT-OSS-20B, a 20-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, on the MLPerf Small MoE Training benchmark under the MXFP4 microscaling format. The recipe combines established techniques from Abecassis, Felix et al. [arXiv:2509.25149] (hybrid 1D/2D block quantization, randomized Hadamard transforms, and stochastic rounding) with a simplified weight de-oscillation scheme adapted from TetraJet-v2 [arXiv:2510.27527]. On C4 validation at global batch size 16, MXFP4 + RHT + SR + de-oscillation reaches a validation loss of 3.3350 at 16,128 steps, only 0.007 above the BF16 baseline (3.3283), closing roughly 50% of the gap left by MXFP4 without de-oscillation (3.3418). Measured by steps to reach the MLPerf quality target (validation loss 3.34), de-oscillation cuts the FP4 convergence overhead relative to BF16 from +20.0% to +5.0%. We also report negative end-to-end results from differential gradient estimation, outlier clipping, and macro-block scaling, despite each showing operator-level SNR gains. All experiments use simulated MXFP4 kernels on AMD MI300X hardware and wall-clock speed has not been optimized.

ai.title: How Does Post-Training Shape LLM Value Preferences?
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.33371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: During post-training, large language models (LLMs) learn value preferences from corpora that may contain imbalanced proportions of opinions associated with different demographic groups. Amplifying these imbalances may further underrepresent some groups' opinions. However, how opinion mixtures shape value preferences across post-training paths remains unclear. To answer this question, we conduct controlled experiments using post-training corpora with different opinion mixtures and five post-training paths based on SFT, DPO, and GRPO. We find that post-training amplifies opinion imbalances differently across post-training paths. Once value preferences are amplified, whether further post-training can remove them depends on both the post-training method and the opinion mixture in the corpus. More concerningly, a model's stability under interventions depends on whether further post-training changes its value preference. Moreover, these value preferences are transferred to student models even when distillation uses corpora with no explicit opinion questions. These findings suggest that both the opinion mixture in post-training corpora and the choice of post-training method should be considered when developing, evaluating, and reusing LLMs. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/ku-nlp/llm-value-preferences.

ai.title: SLICE-Mem: Salience-Gated Lightweight Information Curation for Efficient LLM Agent Memory
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.33015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to maintain personalized and temporally coherent interactions, but repeated LLM inference for memory admission, extraction, and organization introduces substantial cost and latency. We present SLICE-Mem, a lightweight memory framework that combines salience-guided admission and predicate-centered information extraction. A compact classifier identifies user turns worth retaining, and a semantic-dependency-based extractor converts admitted turns into concise memory entries. This online pipeline requires no generative LLM calls, while cross-entry reconciliation is deferred to an offline consolidation stage. We evaluate SLICE-Mem on the weekly subset of Memora and LongMemEval-S using 8B and 30B Qwen backbones for memory construction and consolidation on both benchmarks. Compared with the generative-memory baseline MemOS under the Qwen3-30B configuration, SLICE-Mem's online pipeline achieves 46.60 versus 46.68 FAMA (Forgetting-Aware Memory Accuracy) on Memora Weekly and 56.8% versus 59.3% accuracy on LongMemEval-S, while reducing total LLM token consumption by 92.4% and 99.5%, respectively. These results demonstrate that SLICE-Mem can preserve useful evidence for long-term memory with substantially less reliance on LLM-based memory construction.

trade.title: 海關籲請正確申報統計用數量，提升貿易統計品質
trade.source_name: 財政部關務署 新聞
trade.via: 財政部關務署 新聞
trade.raw_summary: 財政部關務署表示，高品質的海關進出口貿易統計資料，除金額之正確性外，統一的計量單位亦不容忽視。依聯合國國際商品貿易統計手冊建議，同一稅則六碼下貨品應盡量使用相同之數量單位，據此，關務署依各貨品不同屬性，訂定一致性之統計用數量單位，共17種供報關使用，俾利國際規範接軌及提高資料準確度。 關務署指出，進口報單中數量欄位有二種：一為第41欄「數量（單位）」，係計價用數量，請依發票所載交易數量填列；二為第42欄「數量（統計用）」，請依「中華民國海關進口稅則輸出入貨品分類表合訂本」單位欄內所載單位換算後填列，以取得具比較性的數量資料。 關務署舉例說明，部分紡織品之統計用單位為MTK（平方公尺），惟常見之計價單位為碼或英吋，申報時若未將長、寬個別換算為公尺即直接相乘，就會產生誤報情形。以下為常見換算範例，提醒業者注意： 一、碼數換算（1碼=0.9144公尺）：「長1,214碼、寬1.5公尺」之尼龍胚布，應先將長度（碼）轉換為公尺再乘寬，正確計算為 (1,214 × 0.9144) × 1.5 ≒ 1,665.12平方公尺。 二、英吋換算（1英吋=0.0254公尺）：「長300公尺、寬47英吋」之沙發布，應先將寬度（英吋）轉換為公尺，正確算法為 300 × (47 × 0.0254) ≒ 358平方公尺。 關務署籲請業者應正確申報統計用數量，以提升我國貿易統計資料之正確性，該署亦彙整申報統計用數量單位應注意事項及常見錯誤案例，置於海關進出口統計查詢網＞貿易統計＞其他參考資訊＞統計宣導事項( https://portal.sw.nat.gov.tw/APGA/GA17_DEC）＞ 4.統計用數量單位，歡迎民眾及業者多加利用。 新聞稿聯絡人：劉科長 聯絡電話：（02）25505500分機2806

trade.raw_summary: 一、國際經濟情勢 1.IMF及Oxford Economics最新展望，今(2026)年全球經濟成長率分別為3.1%(按購買力平價計算)、2.6%，明年加速至3.4%及2.8%。 2.由於人工智慧(AI)投資需求超乎預期，WTO及IMF均上修國際貿易展望，預測今年全球貿易量分別成長3.9%、4.6%，明年各為4.1%及4.7%。 二、國內經貿情勢 1.隨全球AI投資熱潮持續強勁，加上傳統外銷旺季及產品漲價效應，我國115年第3季出口2,449億美元，進口因AI產業鏈國際分工與出口衍生需求上升，及原物料行情居高，亦達1,817億美元，雙締新猷。資訊電子工業生產指數續揚，年增31.1%，推升製造業、工業生產各增23.0%、21.9%。 2.消費方面，因車市買氣回溫，加上百貨公司新商場加入之集客效應，第3季零售業營業額年增7.6%；餐飲業受惠於暑假與節慶聚餐商機，以及連鎖品牌拓展營業規模，年增3.9%。9月失業率3.36%，終止連續3個月走揚，1-9月平均3.34%，創近26年同期新低。 3.賦稅方面，1-9月實徵淨額3兆5,714億元，為歷年同期新高，年增24.4%，主因股市熱絡推升證交稅收，而營所稅受惠於結算申報自繳及暫繳稅款俱增，營業稅在內需穩定及進口代徵稅款挹注下，表現均佳。稅目中以證交稅增3,077億元最多，營所稅及營業稅分別增1,853億元、1,203億元次之。 三、近年綜合所得稅走勢及申報概況 1.綜所稅稅收在景氣波動與制度變革中維持穩步增長，114年達8,737億元，連續5年刷新紀錄。107年稅制改革為重要轉折點，免稅戶占比大幅上升，113年占總申報戶45%，前20%所得者囊括6成所得總額、貢獻97%稅負。近10年扣除總扣除額後之有效稅率僅介於4%~7%，107年稅改後，占比4成的較低所得者之稅率為零，反映累進稅制及減稅政策的效果。 2.113年總扣除額占所得總額比重約6成，民眾實質租稅負擔減輕；近9成申報戶採標準扣除額，列舉項目集中於醫藥費。前20%所得者具稅務規劃及財富能力，申報捐贈、儲蓄特別扣除額皆約占全體半數。長期照顧特別扣除額申報戶數及金額逐年攀升，113年分別達40萬戶、518億元高點，幼兒學前特別扣除額亦突破千億元，凸顯政府對長照需求及育兒家庭負擔之重視。 3.113年單身申報戶占比達57.4%高峰，且平均每增加10戶納稅戶中就有近8戶為「單身無扶養者」，反映未婚與家庭小型化的普及。人口高齡化使70歲以上受扶養人占比升至27%，近10年劇增8.2個百分點，未滿18歲受扶養人占比則降至37%；而41-50歲族群已成為稅收貢獻重心。面對少子女、高齡與單身化社會，在維持稅基韌性的同時，適度搭配支援家庭照顧及養護的相關措施，將是未來賦稅政策的重要核心。 四、結語 1.中東戰事未歇，美國貿易政策反覆多變，惟AI投資驅動之龐大需求，以及各經濟體展現的因應機制與調適能力，抵消部分負面衝擊，今年以來總體經貿活動運行優於預期。明年全球景氣雖可望延續穩定向上步調，然而地緣政治衝突與貿易摩擦升級、市場重新評估AI發展前景，以及各國財政脆弱性加深等潛在風險，均可能增添國際經濟情勢之不確定性。 2.AI 榮景及科技新品相繼推出，第 3 季我國出口及製造業生產再迎高峰；另就業市場穩定，消費動能維持穩健，加以新車買氣及節慶效應顯現，零售與餐飲營業額齊創同季新高。儘管外部環境變數仍在，惟隨AI效益擴散，且我國位處全球供應鏈關鍵樞紐，有助支撐投資與出口動能，在內、外需雙引擎驅動下，第 4 季國內經濟料將延續上升態勢。 3.今年以來受惠AI商機熱度延續，臺股

trade.title: 國際貿易署更新戰略性高科技貨品出口實體管理名單，新增納管343個涉武擴活動實體
trade.source_name: 經濟部國際貿易署 新聞
trade.via: 經濟部國際貿易署 新聞
trade.raw_summary: 國際貿易署定期召開跨部會審查會議，討論更新戰略性高科技貨品出口實體管理名單。相關更新作業係依貿易法第13條授權，主要參考聯合國安全理事會及友盟國家的制裁與管制名單，迄今已有逾11,660個實體與個人列入該名單。 國際貿易署近日召開跨部會出口實體清單審查會議，基於防止武器擴散、國際制裁考量，於本(22)日發布，新增伊朗、俄羅斯、墨西哥、阿拉伯聯合大公國、土耳其、中國大陸等343個實體及移除90個實體。 國內廠商倘欲出口予我國出口實體名單中受管制實體，應事先取得國際貿易署核發的戰略性高科技貨品輸出許可證，始得憑證出口。另，海關將協助執行邊境攔查，倘有業者在未經許可擬出口實體名單之對象，海關將不予放行。 國際貿易署提醒廠商務必遵守出口管制規範，善盡企業查證之義務，謹慎評估交易風險，以避免涉入武擴活動。該署將持續辦理宣導說明會，協助業者瞭解出口管制規範。 目前戰略性高科技貨品出口實體管名單(總表)，以及本次更新名單，請參考國際貿易署官網：https://www.trade.gov.tw/Pages/Detail.aspx?nodeID=4433&pid=725764 貿易署發言人：胡副署長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7109、02-2397-7178、0966-525-106 業務聯絡人：貿易安全管理辦公室蕭執行秘書 聯絡電話：02-2397-7552
